title: 金高騰の陰で広がる水銀汚染リスク　消費者も問われる水俣の教訓
extracted_text: 1956年に公式確認され「公害の原点」といわれる「水俣病」。高度経済成長期に未曽有の被害と差別を生み、救済の訴えは今も続く。 公式確認から70年を経てなお人々を苦しめる水俣病の苦い経験は、水銀による健康被害や環境汚染を防ぐ国連の「水銀に関する水俣条約」につながった。 「水俣病の問題が長い間解決しない状況で、世界で同じ失敗を繰り返してはいけない。その思いが反映された」。交渉官として条約作りに関わった元環境省水・大気環境局長の早水輝好さんは、2013年に熊本市で開かれた外交会議で採択された意義をそう語る。 早水さんによると、10～13年の政府間交渉委員会の早い段階で、条約を採択する会議を日本で開くことに各国が合意した。条約の名称には、採択した会議の開催地名を冠するのが一般的だ。 「他国からの反対はほぼなかった。国内では名称を『水俣条約』とすることに賛否はあったが、結果的に水俣のことを世界中に知ってもらうきっかけになった」と振り返る。 条約の基本理念を示す前文には「水俣病の重要な教訓を認識し、将来において同様の事態を防止する」と明記された。 日本でも、水銀を含む電池や血圧計、家庭用蛍光灯など18品目の廃止が決まった。今後、歯の治療に用いられる合金「アマルガム」も加わる予定だ。
translated_text: Minamata disease, officially confirmed in 1956 and called the 'origin of pollution', created unprecedented damage and discrimination during Japan's high-growth economic period, and calls for relief continue to this day. The bitter experience of Minamata disease, which continues to torment people even 70 years after official recognition, led to the UN's Minamata Convention on Mercury, aimed at preventing health damage and environmental pollution caused by mercury. 'The thinking that the problem of Minamata disease must not remain unresolved, and the world must not repeat the same failure, is reflected in this.' These were the words of Mr. Hayamizu Teruyoshi, a former director of the Water and Atmospheric Environment Bureau at the Environment Ministry who was involved in crafting the convention, explaining its significance adopted at the diplomatic conference held in Kumamoto City in 2013. According to Mr. Hayamizu, at an early stage of the intergovernmental negotiation committee from 2010 to 2013, all nations agreed to hold the conference to adopt the convention in Japan. It is common for the convention's name to include the location where the adopting conference was held. 'There was virtually no opposition from other countries. Within Japan, there were divided opinions on naming it the Minamata Convention, but in the end it became an opportunity to make Minamata known throughout the world,' he recalled. The preamble setting out the convention's basic principles explicitly states 'recognizing the important lessons of Minamata disease and preventing similar situations in the future.' In Japan, 18 products including batteries containing mercury, blood pressure monitors, and household fluorescent lamps have also been banned. Amalgam, an alloy used for dental treatment, is also scheduled to be added.
title_en: Mercury Pollution Risk Expands in Gold Mining Shadow — Minamata's Lesson Also Questions Consumers
